sourcedFrom: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 (2025)
cleanIntro: The Gen6 strips like every GLOCK before it, and the one step that catches people is unchanged: the slide comes back only about 1/8 inch — 3 mm — before the slide lock comes down. Pull it further and the trigger resets, and a reset trigger means pulling it again before the slide will come off. Two things are Gen6-specific and worth knowing at the bench: the frame takes different backstraps from the V Series, and the magazine catch is reversible, so check which side yours is on before you reach for it in a hurry.

steps.title: ⛔ A forward trigger means the pistol MAY BE LOADED
steps.action: Before anything else: if the trigger is forward, GLOCK's own warning is that the pistol may be loaded. Point the muzzle somewhere safe with your finger off the trigger, press the magazine catch and take the magazine out. Clear all live ammunition off the bench first.
steps.prose: On a striker pistol the trigger position is a state indicator, not a convenience. Read it before you touch anything else.
steps.aside: Remove the magazine by pressing the magazine catch
steps.quote: If the trigger is in the forward position, your GLOCK pistol may be loaded.
steps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Field stripping, printed p.17

steps.title: ⛔ Lock the slide open and check the chamber by EYE and by FINGER
steps.action: Grasp the slide at the rear serrations, pull it fully back to eject anything in the chamber, then push up on the slide stop lever and ease the slide forward until it locks open. Now look into the chamber AND put a finger in it, and check the magazine well the same way. The loaded-chamber indicator is a mechanical device and GLOCK says plainly it can fail.
steps.prose: Two senses, two places. The indicator is not one of the two.
steps.caution: Never rely solely on a loaded chamber indicator or your memory to determine whether your GLOCK pistol is loaded or unloaded. Always retract the slide by grasping it at the serrations at the rear of the slide and pulling it fully to the rear and pushing up on the slide stop lever to lock the slide open, and then visually and physically (with your finger) check to make sure there is not a cartridge in the chamber.
steps.aside: Once the slide is locked to the rear, both visually and physically (with your finger) inspect both the chamber and the magazine well of the pistol to be sure that no ammunition remains in either place
steps.quote: Lock the slide in the rearward (open) position by pushing up on the slide stop lever (27) and slowly releasing the slide from the fully rearward position until it locks in the open position
steps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Field stripping, printed p.18

steps.title: ⛔ Trigger pulled on the EMPTY pistol — the order is mandatory
steps.action: Release the slide forward, and with the muzzle in a safe direction pull the trigger. The striker has to be down before the slide will come off. GLOCK states that to ensure the pistol is unloaded the disassembly MUST be performed in its order — the clearing steps above are what make this one safe.
steps.prose: Every part of this procedure that looks like ceremony is the part that proves the gun is empty.
steps.quote: To field strip (disassemble) your GLOCK pistol for cleaning, follow the instructions below. To ensure that your GLOCK pistol is unloaded, disassembly MUST be performed in this order.
steps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Field stripping, printed p.18

steps.title: ⛔ Slide back 1/8 in. / 3 mm ONLY — further resets the trigger
steps.action: Take the pistol in your firing hand with your fingers across the top of the slide in front of the rear sight and your thumb on the rear of the frame. Retract the slide about 1/8 inch — 3 mm — and hold it there. Go further and the trigger resets; if that happens, keep the muzzle safe and pull the trigger again before continuing.
steps.prose: Three millimetres. It is a smaller movement than almost anyone expects, and it is why people end up doing this step twice.
steps.caution: If you pull the slide too far to the rear, it will reset the pistol's trigger to the forward position. If this happens, while keeping the muzzle of your GLOCK pistol pointed in a safe direction, pull the trigger again)
steps.quote: Using your fingers, retract the slide (1) about 1/8 in. / 3mm and hold it in this position
steps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Field stripping, printed p.19

steps.title: Slide lock DOWN evenly on both sides, slide forward off the frame
steps.action: With the slide held back those 3 mm, use the thumb and index finger of your other hand to pull the slide lock down EVENLY on both sides. Keep it down and push the slide forward off the front of the frame.
steps.prose: Evenly is the operative word. One side down and one side half-down is what makes a slide feel stuck and invites force.
steps.quote: pull the slide lock (21) down evenly on both sides
steps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Field stripping, printed p.19

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly: press toward the MUZZLE, lift out
steps.action: Press the recoil spring assembly toward the muzzle end of the slide while pulling it up and out. It is captive but under load — keep a thumb on it rather than letting it jump.
steps.prose: Forward first, then up. Lifting straight out binds it against its seat.
steps.quote: Press the recoil spring assembly (3) toward the front (muzzle end) of the slide while pulling it up to remove it from the slide
steps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Field stripping, printed p.19

steps.title: Barrel out: lift by the locking cams, forward, then up and rearward
steps.action: Hold the barrel by the barrel locking cams, lift it and push it toward the front of the slide, then pull it up and toward the rear to bring it clear. That is the field strip: five components — frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly and magazine.
steps.prose: GLOCK counts five main components for cleaning. Five on the mat means you are done, not that you have stopped early.
steps.aside: To clean your GLOCK pistol, first disassemble it into its five main components
steps.quote: Holding the barrel by the barrel locking cams, lift it and push it toward the front of the slide and then pull it up and toward the rear to remove it from the slide
steps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Field stripping, printed p.20

steps.title: ⛔ NEVER go further — and two things not to do while it is apart
steps.action: GLOCK's instruction is explicit: never disassemble further; anything beyond this is for a GLOCK-Certified Armorer and doing it otherwise voids the warranty. While the pistol is apart, do not manually reset the trigger forward and then pull it, and do not pull the firing pin back and let it snap forward — each damages the safety it works against.
steps.prose: Both of those are things people do idly, with the slide in one hand, without thinking of them as disassembly at all.
steps.caution: When your GLOCK pistol is disassembled, never manually reset the trigger to its forward position and then pull it to the rear because this could damage the trigger safety.
steps.aside: do not manually pull the firing pin (4) to the rear of the slide and allow it to snap forward because this could damage the firing pin and the firing pin safety
steps.quote: Never further disassemble your GLOCK pistol (Picture 24). Any further disassembly must be performed by a GLOCK-Certified Armorer.
steps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Field stripping, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Five components, and no more
deepSteps.action: GLOCK's cleaning routine begins by disassembling into the five main components — nothing in the routine requires going past them. If a cleaning instruction seems to need a sixth part in your hand, it is not this manual's instruction.
deepSteps.prose: The count is the boundary, stated as a count so it is hard to argue with.
deepSteps.quote: To clean your GLOCK pistol, first disassemble it into its five main components
deepSteps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Preventive maintenance, printed p.23

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Do not snap the firing pin while the slide is off
deepSteps.action: With the pistol disassembled, do not pull the firing pin to the rear of the slide and let it snap forward. GLOCK states it can damage the firing pin and the firing pin safety. There is nothing to arrest it out of the gun.
deepSteps.prose: It is a satisfying noise and an expensive one. The same applies to resetting the trigger by hand.
deepSteps.aside: When your GLOCK pistol is disassembled, never manually reset the trigger to its forward position and then pull it to the rear because this could damage the trigger safety.
deepSteps.quote: do not manually pull the firing pin (4) to the rear of the slide and allow it to snap forward because this could damage the firing pin and the firing pin safety
deepSteps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Field stripping, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Gen6 backstraps and a reversible magazine catch
deepSteps.action: The Gen6 and the V Series take different backstraps, and the Gen6 magazine catch is reversible. If you have changed either, confirm the backstrap is seated and the catch is on the side you expect before the pistol goes back into service — and unload the pistol before changing a backstrap.
deepSteps.prose: A magazine catch on the unexpected side is a problem you discover at the worst possible moment.
deepSteps.quote: The V Series and Gen6 come with different backstraps and a reversible magazine catch to customize your pistol.
deepSteps.cite: GLOCK SAFE ACTION® PISTOLS — INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE (Gen6) — EN 10-25 — printed on page 1; document 51959, relaunch standard Gen6 — Pistol customizing, printed p.34

cleaning.name: BARREL AND BORE
tasks: Run a bore brush and solvent from the CHAMBER end, then patch until the patches come out clean.
Wipe the outside of the barrel, and pay attention to the locking cams and the lug — that is where fouling and wear both show.

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Brush the breech face, the extractor claw and the slide rails.
⛔ Keep solvent and fouling OUT of the firing-pin channel — on a striker pistol that channel wants to be dry.

cleaning.name: FRAME AND RECOIL ASSEMBLY
tasks: Wipe the frame rails and the magazine well; check the slide lock returns under its own spring on both sides.
Wipe the recoil spring assembly down; it is captive and stays assembled.
⚠ Gen6 frames take different backstraps from the V Series and the magazine catch is reversible — make sure whatever you removed goes back the way it was.

reassembly: Barrel into the slide first, seated on its locking cams.
Recoil spring assembly in, pressed toward the muzzle and dropped into its seat.
Slide onto the frame rails and run it fully back; the slide lock returns on its own.
⛔ Do NOT manually reset the trigger while the pistol is apart.
Function-check before the pistol goes away.
fncheck: With the pistol CLEAR: rack the slide several times and watch it return fully to battery under spring pressure alone. Check the slide lock rises and falls freely on both sides. With the gun empty and pointed safely, pull the trigger for a clean break, then hold it back, cycle the slide, release and listen for the reset click. Insert an EMPTY magazine and confirm the slide locks back on the slide stop lever.
